summary.text: Early forms of 元 are interpreted as a human figure with a mark at the head. The graph is associated with ‘head’; oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions also use it for ‘first’ or ‘beginning.’

formation.text: Pictographic: early forms are interpreted as a human figure whose head is marked by a point or square, sometimes reduced to a horizontal stroke. This is a reading of the whole image, not a confirmed division into modern components. The received 說文 analysis connects 元 with 一 and 兀; later interpreters disagreed whether 兀 supplied a sound or the sense ‘head.’ A separate proposal reads the upper strokes as 上 over 人, but this is challenged by the point-marked early forms.

history.text: Early graph forms are catalogued in oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript, seal-script, and Qin-slip contexts. The curated seal-script image is a modern redraw in the style associated with 說文, not an ancient artifact or an image of the earliest head-marked forms; no stroke-by-stroke sequence is asserted here.
The proposal that 元 and 兀 split from one graph is not established as 元’s origin. The received 說文 breakdown and later disagreement over 兀 likewise do not settle the graph’s original construction.

uncertainties.text: The early head-marked pictorial interpretation is supported, but identifying its strokes specifically as 儿 plus 二 is not established. The alternative 上-over-人 analysis is disputed.
The graph’s proposed head referent does not establish the original spoken word or its pronunciation. The exact semantic path among ‘head,’ ‘first/beginning,’ and ‘great’ is also unresolved.
Exact dates for the cited oracle-bone and bronze examples are unresolved. The transmitted 左傳 and 孟子 quotations attest textual uses, not dated manuscript witnesses.

senses.text: Early forms are interpreted as depicting a human head. The cited oracle-bone and bronze examples use 元 for other meanings; ‘head’ occurs in transmitted 左傳 and 孟子 passages.

senses.period: oracle-bone and Western Zhou bronze contexts; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: An oracle-bone example 元卜 is interpreted as ‘first divination,’ and a Western Zhou bronze inscription uses 元 in 元年, ‘first year.’ These are early attested uses; they do not establish priority over every other sense.

senses.period: bronze inscriptional use; exact date unresolved
senses.text: The bronze phrase 元德 is interpreted as ‘great virtue.’ Its relation to ‘head’ or ‘first/beginning’ is unresolved.

developments.text: A development from ‘head’ to ‘first/beginning’ has been proposed, but the available examples do not document a dated sequence for that change.

limitations.text: The pictorial interpretation proposes a referent; it does not by itself establish the original spoken meaning. The chronology among ‘head,’ ‘first/beginning,’ and ‘great’ is incomplete.
‘Origin’ and ‘dollar’ appear among the supplied glosses, but no historical attestations or development account are provided for them.

overview.text: 元 is interpreted as an early picture of a person with the head marked. It is associated with ‘head’ and is attested in inscriptions meaning ‘first’ or ‘beginning’; the link between those meanings is uncertain.
